The gate's own acceptance criteria (pm-e6tm5c) classify changes as additive, compatible or breaking, but no signature change is ever classed as compatible. The cost: breaking_acknowledgements fills with false positives, which hides the real breaks reviewers and release notes must see. Proposal: classify signature changes by position. A new optional property on an object type is compatible. A new required property on a type the caller supplies, or any removed property, is breaking. A return type widened from void, and a parameter made optional, are compatible. Keep a removed export and a narrowed input as breaking. Record the classification reason with each change. Found while landing pm-wb6ktl (2026-11-16). scripts/sdk-surface-snapshot.mjs compares each exported symbol's printed signature text, and any difference is reported as breaking. Adding an optional, host-set field to BeforeMutationHookContext was reported as breaking. That context is built by the host and handed to guards, and no implementer constructs it, so no consumer is affected. As a result, an additive SDK change needs the same recorded acknowledgement as a removed export. The gate's own acceptance criteria (pm-e6tm5c) classify changes as additive, compatible or breaking, but no signature change is ever classed as compatible. The cost is that breaking_acknowledgements fill with false positives, which hides the real breaks that reviewers and release notes must see. Some widenings are genuinely breaking, so the classifier must not over-correct. During the same PR, widening runRegisteredMutationGuardForTest from Promise<void> to a value-bearing promise broke consumers that return it from a Promise<void> function (TS2322). An optional property added to a type the caller supplies breaks a caller value that already carries a same-named property of an incompatible type. Proposal: classify signature changes by position and kind, and record the reason with each change. These are compatible: a new optional property on a type only the host constructs; an optional property added to a caller-supplied type when no caller can already carry a same-named, differently typed property; a plain void return widened; a parameter made optional. These stay breaking: removed exports or properties; a new required property on a caller-supplied type; an added optional property that can conflict with a caller's existing same-named property; a Promise<void> or other non-plain-void return widened to a value-bearing type; a narrowed input. author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: A signature change is classified compatible only when generated consumer probes (assignment, implementation, keyof and return-use positions) that compile against the old declarations also compile against the new ones; otherwise it is breaking; Each breaking classification records the failing probe as its reason, and each compatible one records the probes it passed; The spec corpus includes every PR 1740 counterexample as a negative control: Promise<void> widening, void-to-value return, a conflicting optional property, a keyof-derived consumer, and a callback parameter made optional; A host-built context gaining an optional field passes as compatible when no probe breaks, so the BeforeMutationHookContext case needs no acknowledgement

Found while landing pm-wb6ktl (2026-11-16). scripts/sdk-surface-snapshot.mjs compares each exported symbol's printed signature text, and any difference is reported as breaking. Adding an optional, host-set field to BeforeMutationHookContext was reported as breaking, so an additive SDK change needs the same recorded acknowledgement as a removed export. The gate's own acceptance criteria (pm-e6tm5c) classify changes as additive, compatible or breaking, but no signature change is ever classed as compatible. As a result, breaking_acknowledgements fill with false positives, which hides the real breaks that reviewers and release notes must see. Reviews of PR 1740 showed that hand-written variance rules cannot fix this, because each rule has a counterexample: Promise<void> widened to a value-bearing promise; a plain void return changed to a value, which breaks `const result: void = f()`; an optional property that conflicts with a same-named, differently typed property a caller value already carries; an optional property that changes keyof-derived types such as Record<keyof Context, string>; and a callback parameter made optional, which breaks implementations that require it under strict function types. Proposal: classify by proof, not by rule. A change is compatible only when the classifier proves that every consumer program in a declared corpus still type-checks after the change, for example by compiling generated consumer probes (assignment, implementation, keyof and return-use positions) against both declaration sets. Anything it cannot prove stays breaking, with the failing probe recorded as the reason.
